page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-16 is an Arm-based virtual machine configuration within Google Cloud. It is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 architecture and provides 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs. All storage operations rely on external persistent network disk volumes, and standard public IPv4 networking requires separately configured addressing.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, the instance emphasizes memory capacity per compute unit. The arm64 processor design delivers energy-efficient compute cycles with dedicated vCPU allocation, ensuring consistent CPU performance without hyper-threading contention. However, workloads requiring local NVMe storage for low-latency scratch space or x86 instruction sets will face tradeoffs, as the environment relies exclusively on network-attached storage and the 64-bit Arm ISA. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density allows consolidation of memory-heavy tasks onto fewer cores, reducing per-core licensing and compute overhead.

The resource distribution makes the c4a-highmem-16 suited for workloads that demand substantial memory capacity relative to compute footprint. Typical use cases include in-memory databases, caching layers, medium-scale data analytics, memory-intensive containerized services, and compilation pipelines targeted at Arm architectures.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-16 is an arm64 virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory. Operating with an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, the instance is engineered for memory-intensive operations within an energy-efficient Arm architecture. The configuration includes no local storage or onboard graphics processing units, necessitating reliance on network-attached persistent storage for filesystem operations. Dedicated vCPU provisioning provides consistent execution without hyper-threading competition, while the absence of bundled disks offers architectural flexibility for attaching network volumes tailored to specific IO requirements. The high memory-to-core allocation provides qualitative resource efficiency by supporting large working sets without requiring an excessive number of compute cores. Consequently, the c4a-highmem-16 configuration is appropriate for in-memory caching platforms, memory-bound database engines, medium-scale data processing pipelines, and Arm64 software development environments.
